items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I didn't. And a heck of a lot of people didn't. You know. That chick, she didn't care about it still today. She don't care about a lot of the men, you know, Mary Lou Williams.

ctx.x: And yet there are so few women in brass players, or reed players. Why is that, in jazz?

I don't know, because to me there's no such animal, until I met Dyer. I'd never heard of a -- well, you saw -- when I was a kid you'd see a woman who played piano, played in church. Ding, ding-da-ding. Church piano. You know what I mean. They -- 'Come to Jesus,' I mean that's a song that we always -- [Mamie] always said, it didn't sound like anything. And later years, I mean all the way up to Mary Lou Williams.
